I tried.  Quite a few times over the years.  No.

It's not that I have a problem with co-op shooters, especially the loot shoot kind since the bane of my existence seems to be the Borderlands franchise or similar, but I've never been terribly fond of this one no matter how much I force myself to get acclimated to it.  Despite knowing a few friends that have this that still do play it, and wanting to take some time to get better to have fun with it, that opinion continues to remain unchanged.  There's really nothing I like in the few hours I've seen that I'm willing to play or practice on to get any better at.  Much of what I see appears to be a pretty same-y loop that just isn't interesting and borders on annoying more than anything.

What I do hear from people that have hundreds of hours more on it than myself is how generally frustrating it is once you decide to increase the difficulty which is probably even worse - we go from one annoyance to another.  Put that all together and it gives me little reason to pursue it with such a vocal amount telling me otherwise.  Even though they play it.

Which isn't weird to me I suppose.  I do play Mahjong.  I do have a masochist streak to me in some things but I'd rather not expand on that with this title.

Anyways, that could be unique to me but when I browse other reviews I seem to find a common ground on that, especially as of late.  I wish I could say better.  It's one of those things that I wish I could be part of the 'overwhelmingly positive' crowd but sadly there's just nothing here that hooks me to do so.

claims.claim: The game can feel overwhelming to beginners due to the large amount of systems and content going on.

citations.review_text: So much fun with a group of friends. Deep Rock Galactic has a lot going on for it now, which can be overwhelming if you are just starting off, but once you find the right place to begin, the gameplay really clicks. This is a solid game.

I'm still learning what everything does as the game has a lot of things to learn.

The controls are responsive, sound effects are good, weapons handle well, lots of character customisation, different builds for each character, different weapon combo's, good mission variation with various enemies that can attack while mining an area or returning to the mule.

They will also attack when returning to the pod once a mission is complete.

After each successful mission your character earns XP to level up, which will unlock other missions or areas to explore.

It's quite an addictive game.  Get in, mine what you can and get out, hopefully, in one piece. :D

I'm enjoying what I've played so far, but I have a lot more to learn.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features procedural generation and variable levels, ensuring that missions do not feel identical.

citations.review_text: One of the best hoard shooters of all time. Does not disappoint with its missions, gameplay and every level feels new. So far I am really enjoying it. ROCK AND STONE!!!!!!

I liked this game, the controls are simple and easy to pick up. I grew up on console and it only took me a few minutes to master the controls playing this on PC. The gameplay is fun and the generated levels are interesting.

Was so good, I bought it twice. Once on console during season 2 and now this time to get mods and multiplayer access without a subscription. As of right now, I have easily dumped 9 hours into this game in one day even after playing the game for years on console. Procedural generation and an amazing community make this game endlessly replayable alone even without all the progression mechanics and loadout possibilities.

Only 12hrs in but this game is a blast. The level design / gameplay loop is super fun and stays fresh since no two missions are the same. The hub area is top-tier, and the progression is super addicting. I see myself getting many more hours in this. Rock and stone!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that previous season passes remain accessible to progress through without missing out on items.

citations.review_text: one of the more fun games i've played. i really like the way the battlepass things work because you can go to previous seasons.

It is a very fun game that doesn't think about money at all. This game has a season pass but it is for free and you can go into the previous seasons to not miss out on anything. It is a very enjoyable game that is clearly made with the intent of being fun for the customer.

There's not much I can say that the other overwhelmingly positive reviews already didn't cover. The game is probably my favorite of its kind. You pick a procedurally generated mission and launch into a procedurally generated map and do that mission while also mining around for ore and gold to buy some cosmetics and upgrades.

90% of the progression is cosmetic. On top of that, there is NO FOMO when it comes to cosmetics (except for anniversary hats) ALL cosmetics are unlockable and ALL previous season passes are still available for you to progress through. 

The game gets updated almost constantly and there's enough content to last you hundreds of hours. 

Also, I think I ♥♥♥♥♥♥ around in the lobby more than actually playing the game. Why is there a functional prop hunt minigame there?? Amazing.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features minigames and interactive elements in the lobby, such as drinking beer and playing prop hunt.

citations.review_text:
top 5 reasons to play deep rock galactic:

Maps always feel different. 
You can drink beer.
You can pass out from drinking too much beer. 
You can play flappy bird. 
You can find jet boots in some games. Yes jet boots. Dwarf will fly. 


Honorable mention: the OST SLAPS

ROCK AND STONE!

This is a game that you can have a lot of fun on by both playing with friends [b]or[/b] by yourself. There's lots of stuff to do and the progression feels good. [Might feel a little slow at first. But once you get a hang of it, it will feel good.] The learning curve is good, however things might feel a little overwhelming at first. But you'll get up to speed pretty quickly!

I can personally play on Level 3 difficulty with no issues, Level 4 can be pretty challenging playing Solo. Depending on what mission type it is. [There are 5 levels of difficulties. 1-5]
You can also do lots of fun stuff in the mission control, by playing small mini games and drinking beer until you pass out! And the game it self is also pretty goofy!

[h3]Each mission feels different[/h3]
You have quite a few different mission [b]types[/b] and each mission has a secondary goal that will give you some extra bonus points! While some missions could also contain some hidden loot. So keep your eyes peeled!

[h3]In conclusion:[/h3]
I'm having lots of fun playing this game. It's a game that I can kick back, relax, shut my brain off, while keep my focus sharp. And it's not like it's the end of the world if I fail a mission either. So it's a good balance of keeping you focused in the game, but also do stuff without much thinking.

[b]Rock and Stone eveyone![/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the monetization model is free of aggressive practices, featuring cosmetic-only DLCs and no premium currencies or pay-to-win elements.

citations.review_text: This game is a ton of fun. You can pick it up and play solo, join a game real easy, and the community is really positive and fun. All the maps are always different due to the procedural generation and the environment is completely destructable. Its fun to just chill and mine and do missions on easy or go Hardcore and get crazy. This is one of my favorite games of all time. The devs are really good and care about the community and game, and they also dont make you pay for season passes, just the cosmetic DLC if you want. All around this game is an 11/10.

it's good game. monetization is minimally predatory (i.e. no gameplay features are locked behind purchases, there is no premium currency). can be a little repetitive but sometimes that's what you want in a game

I truly believe that this game has the nicest community any game could ever have. 
When starting, no knowing anything about the game, enemies, weapons, upgrade system, and common uses among players, other experienced players (graybeards) picked me up, teached me the ways of the game, what to do in what situations, useful tips and what is expected of different classes during missions. 
Like saying "r" (short for "ready") in chat before proceeding in the mission, (driller) put C4 on top of the caretaker to blow up its weak points, always equipping Iron Will, picking up Doretta's head to bring it back, the engineer having to put platforms for the scout under minerals, the gunner putting shields on fallen teammates to revive them, and driller digging straight back to the drop pod when the mission ends.

After 120 hours in this game, I finally had a bad encounter with another player. 
Said encounter wasn't even that bad, i just got kicked out of the game because the owner and I kept calling Molly despite being 100+m away from each other. 
In 120 hours, i NEVER encountered a mean person, sometimes people that just don't say much or do much, but mostly supportive people. I never got scolded, but just got advices. 

I just wanted to review this part of the game, but there is many many other things i could speak about, like the fact that the game weighs only 3 Gb, the fact that all previous seasons and their cosmetics are available for free, the amazing weapon upgrade system, etc etc.

Best 9 bucks i ever spent, I now understand the graybeards that bought the DLC just to support the developers.

Amazing game that actually did the season pass system good! No pay-to-advance system for the pass, no greedy corporate tactics, and all of the paid DLCs are simply cosmetic packs that can be gotten as a way to further support the devs! 10/10, would Rock and Stone again! Also, looking forwards to DRG: Rogue Core, sounds like it'll be just as amazing as DRG!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is exceptionally well-optimized and runs smoothly on low-end hardware with a small installation size.

citations.review_text: If you're here from Helldivers, just know that Deep Rock Galactic has been running an Ironman marathon since 2020 so that Helldivers could sprint briefly into the spotlight.  Deep Rock has been solid and continues to be an absolute blast without requiring a top-tier rig to run.  It's just fantastic little game that keeps on giving.

Shoot bugs and mine as a dwarf without the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ optimization choices of other developers. It is cheap, well optimized as in terms of storage AND performance, you can sink hours in it without being bored at all and it has an amazing community. Simple yet effective progression system with very good endgame choices. Amazing voice acting, remarkable character direction and very enchanting visual design. This is what passion without hesitation looks like. FOR KARL!

Let me get the one negative thing about this game out of the way first. Would dwarves be jumping around everywhere to avoid getting hit by bugs or would they dig a bunker, funnel the bugs through a choke, and kill them efficiently? In higher difficulties you forego immersing yourself into the role of a dwarf and start sprinting and jumping around everywhere to survive and that just totally takes me out of it and back into sweating on fortnite.

What are the positives about this game? LITERALLY EVERYTHING ELSE. 
-No aggressive monetization
-No fear of missing out on limited time gameplay and cosmetics
-No RTX5090 levels of recommended hardware, quite the opposite. The game runs VERY well
-Play the game your own way with your own class and your own build at your own difficulty
-Slow and steady pacing of upgrade and overclock unlocks allowing you to enjoy the gameplay for longer
-Your own skills at navigating caves and the different classes improves while you unlock upgrades
-Teamwork is strongly encouraged by the different classes fulfilling different roles
-Forced teamwork leads to brotherhood and no one ever crashes out
-Solo play is still fun at the right difficulty with an AI companion
-Beautiful visuals when you have a calm moment, varied biomes and cave layouts

I could gush about this game probably a bit more than this list but I wouldn't need any more convincing. Don't miss out on this game, I will look back on this as part of the Golden Age of Co-op game resurgence.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that higher difficulties in solo play become unbalanced and unplayable due to an unreliable AI drone companion.

citations.review_text:
It is a fun game, but if you want to play it solo, the higher difficulties are basically unplayable. The enemies gets  stronger obviously, but you are left with the same stupid "Bosco" drone, that did not get better, stronger or anything. Enemies attacking you? Bosco sometimes just look and don't shoot and let the enemies go directly to you, then starts firing 2-3 seconds after being in full combat. Sometimes the drone just goes hunting somewhere, while you are left alone to defend mission objective. It gets (only) 2 rockets, but you have to tell it when and where to fire it. In the co-op, you are team of four, but In the solo you are team of one + unreliable drone against same odds. I mean, higher difficulties should be challenging, but in solo your skill matters less then the RNG deciding how the map plays.

Over all - do you want to play it with others? Great! You want solo? For beginning yes, but later on, meh. I will recommend the game, because the fun IS there.

[h1]Me and my friends been loving the latest "well crafted" new events the new team have been making on the clearly intended "difficulty" that the devs made![/h1]

Okay I have been holding this review in work for almost three years. 
But every time I opened this page, I feel like I keep getting distracted by new hats, or paints that I kept telling myself I will use. I'm not sure what that says about this game in particular, this ramble is what this game deserves. Rerrr! 

[h1]I would highly recommend this game if you do have 3 spare dwagons near you that you can dognap.[/h1]
[h2]Desc[/h2]
Deep Rock is a very simple game where some company sends you, 4 dwarfs to HOXXES IV to mine and shoot the same bugs. Again. and Again. And then get distracted by some shinies.
(...)
(Also also, if you really like playing alone instead. You can still do that and maybe PET the lootbugs along the way. They are STUPIDLY ROUND and make silly noises. Maybe you can also ask your assistant, Bosco that would at least would NEVER complain about it to help you .. hold Alt-Fire to mine gray rocks. They can also help by staring at you while some ceiling Cave Leech nibbles your muzzle and stuff, owo. So,, Its all worth it. I prolly need to play Solo Haz5+ to amplify the incredibly fun experience. The increased cave complexity +3, infinite insect swarm, and warnings sounds super fun! I love Bosco with its silly "..." voicelines. Mayb its a little shy.

[h2]THINGIES[/h2]
Some do say that the procedural map generation is not exactly exciting. But I do like the consistency of seeing Molley (your personal MULE) gaining the ability to float really makes sense. It keeps the game exciting and full of surprises. I like how many gray rocks there are in HOXXES too, I helped to distract me from noticing the amount of time I got lost in the caves. I would also like to mention how you can bring Doretta head's home with you. What a feature certainly worth mentioning! Now that is the best addition yet since the…

claims.claim: Reviewers complain that recent game updates and new content have slowed down significantly while developers focus resources on spin-off titles.

citations.review_text:
I feel inclined to leave a review and it saddens me to leave this as a negative after so many hours dedicated to DRG. DRG is an amazing game especially with friends. This game does pretty much everything right.

- It's extremely fun and even more enjoyable with friends.
- I never felt myself getting bored especially after getting all the overclocks and despite the biomes being repetitive.
- Being able to muck around in the lobby whilst waiting for people to join is a cornerstone of the DRG experience and the game wouldn't be the same without it.

However, I'm leaving a negative review because the developers who I once held in high esteem have turned out to be very disappointing, and this started with Season 6. From memory as I have not played very often recently, Season 6 was a very long wait, as far as I know this was because Rogue Core development was the main focus. This was annoying but I understood nonetheless. Season 6 came and it was just... well there's not much to say about it. We waited all that time for one new mission type and a new biome that introduced two boring and mildy irritating enemies, particularly the scrabs, which are total ammo dumps and don't seem to leave you alone for the entirery of the mission no matter how many you kill; and worse, zero new weapon overclocks.

What cemented my distaste was after all this time, after all this waiting, Rogue Core like its predecessor Survivor, turned out to be a complete flop that died almost immediately. All the time spent neglecting DRG was for nothing, and whilst I understand and accept that DRG is a complete game and we are not entitled to expect new content; it still left a sour taste in my mouth.

As far as 'content' goes, the only things ever added now are new cosmetic packs and lets be honest, with the exception of a select few like Rival Tech, most of them are not that great anyway, at least in my opinion. On top of this, the only news I see concerning DRG outside of seasonal cosmetics (that aren…

Deep rock galactic is one of my favorite video games of all time.
The game is alot of fun, a big amount of missions with alot of creative enemies, events and guns to play around with.
All of that in fully destructable procedurally generated caves, this game is genuinely amazing.
You can customize your dwarves (the characters you play) alot, so theres alot of freedom to roleplay with.
Every single class plays completely differently and their gameplay changes even more.
Theres alot of strategy that goes in with how you build your loadout wich is alot of fun too.
The main game has insane modding support (the mod browser is built into the game) wich reach from simple additions to whole game overhauls.
Its a perfect game for people who love PvE games that have alot of RnG elements that positively affect the game.
Its also perfect for people who dont have any friends to play with because the game gives a pretty helpful little drone named bosco to help you mine stuff and defend yourself.
My mine issue with the game is that it barely gets any gameplay content updates, i get Ghost ship games is very busy with developing their new game and publishing other games but the last season was 6 months ago and it barely added anything impactful besides a new biome and mission type (wich i guess is alot more than some other content updates but its still very weak).
The game has alot of content to keep you busy for alot of time plus its alot of fun with friends but still i wished the devs would make a few more content updates every year, i dont want to wait another year for a single new mission type and a few new enemies.
But even if that makes you a bit icky on buying the game, please consider buying it still, its alot of fun and i cant recommend it more. 
Thank you ghost ship games for making this game, it means alot to me genuinely. <3

If I were to be writing this review like two years ago, I would've recommended it. But right now it's in a rough state due to sheer neglect by the devs ever since they decided to focus on unnecessary spinoffs instead of polishing and improving their main title.

First of all, lack of updates and fixes. This game barely gets anything worthy these days because they were working on two other lackluster spinoffs that are literally just cashgrabs. This game got so many bugs (no pun intended) that haven't been fixed yet. They ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over the spawnrate so bad that literally some missions can go by smoothly and other times it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There is no consistency whatsover.


Some mission types are so imbalanced like heavy extraction where they have normal horde spawns on top of the horde that spawns when you extract a resinite mass or normal extraction where there is literally a barrage of constant enemies coupled with the normal hordes which forces you to complete the mission as fast as possible to not waste resources. The new enemies that they added in the last few seasons are just plain bad, stingtails are cancerous to fight against (they used to be worse), pitjaws will bring you down to the deepest pits of hell. The devs were like: "Hmm, we have an enemy that spawns on the ceiling so that we force players to look up, how about we make an enemy that is hidden in the ground, ten times tankier, can relocate when it's damaged and not killed, and ten times more plentiful." Genius design.

The grinding in this game, while grindy by design, is executed in the worst way possible. You have a system called weapon overclocks which can either add upgrades to your weapons or make em slightly better, or change the function of the weapon. Neat system and all. However, the method of obtaining those overclocks is so abysmal and takes so damn long to obtain every single one, it is also dedicated by rng, so you don't even have the choice to obtain a specific overclock that you've heard f…

I genuinely love Deep Rock Galactic. I’ve put hundreds of hours into it, bought cosmetics, convinced friends to play it, and defended the game for years because it used to feel like one of the few co-op games made by developers who actually cared.

But now it honestly feels abandoned.

Instead of properly supporting the game that built the community, the studio seems more interested in chasing trends with spin-offs like Survivor — which is basically “Vampire Survivors but with dwarves” — and now Rogue Core, which feels like another attempt to turn DRG into a roguelite instead of improving the original game people actually fell in love with.

Meanwhile the base game barely gets meaningful updates anymore. Not even regular balance tweaks, quality-of-life passes, weapon reworks, bugfixes, or hotfixes at the pace you’d expect from a live-service co-op game this popular. There are bugs and issues that sit around forever while development focus clearly goes elsewhere.

And before people spam “the game already has enough content” — that’s not the point. The point is that the original DRG became successful because of the gameplay loop, teamwork, and constant support. Now it feels like that support has slowed to a crawl while the brand gets stretched into side projects.

I’m not even saying Rogue Core or Survivor are terrible games. I’m saying it sucks watching the original game slowly lose momentum while the developers move on to copy-and-paste trend chasing.

DRG deserved better long-term support than this.

Rock and Stone… I guess.
